key_insight: Integral constraints can improve PINN accuracy by restoring uniform control over error components that standard losses constrain only weakly in certain PDE parameter regimes.
engineering_relevance: Adding integral constraints is most useful when the governing PDE and its parameters leave important solution errors weakly controlled by the standard PINN loss.
method: Add constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the PINN loss.
Derive and compare stability estimates with and without integral constraints for several PDEs.
Test predicted accuracy differences through numerical experiments.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments show clear accuracy differences in regimes predicted to have weak standard-loss control, but similar accuracy when that control remains sufficient.
watch_item: Benefits are parameter-dependent; integral constraints should not be assumed to improve accuracy across all PDEs or regimes.
paper_title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
